synopsis: RACER pursues high-speed autonomous military ground-vehicle driving over unstructured off-road terrain; its relevance here is off-road simulation, not demonstrated construction or mining use [f15829, f15889]. RACER-Sim was announced in January 2022 with Duality Robotics and Intel-Federal as primes, a reported Phase 1 budget of about USD 6 million, and a task for Duality with Neya Systems to build an 80 km² environment measuring 20 km by 4 km [f8419, f8420, f8421]. NASA JPL contracted Duality for RACER Phase II in September 2024, documenting government use and supporting the feasibility of large virtual job sites [f8422, f15839]. This does not establish acceptance of simulation as braking safety evidence: Chapter 2 found no documented RACER precedent with quantified simulation substitution, while Chapter 13 retained RACER as an unverified lead worth checking [f15840, f1427, f11274]. Separately, the booklet uses DARPA's Heilmeier questions and phase go/no-go metrics as planning and review analogues, rather than as braking-validation evidence [f16460, f9909, f15840].
